prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one ORIGINAL MASTER painting for one Bhagavad Gita verse in a Sanskrit reader. Generate a single square 1:1 image, 2048x2048 or the highest actually supported native square resolution. Consistent series style: refined traditional Indian watercolor and restrained gouache on warm ivory handmade paper; fine organic detail, subtle ochre, sage, dusty terracotta and muted indigo; dignified ancient Indian setting, quiet atmospheric daylight. The image must illustrate THIS VERSE'S ACTUAL MEANING. Read the exact source meaning below; derive a concrete, intelligible scene or a restrained symbolic interpretation of that teaching. Never simply paint an unrelated chariot, generic temple or anonymous landscape. Compose one coherent scene, no collage or infographic. Keep important faces, hands, relationships and narrative objects inside the central 60% of width and central 50% of height, surrounded by ample low-detail sky, ground and paper atmosphere. No important subject cut by an edge. This one master must support portrait/landscape phones and tablets through safe proportional fitting. No text of any kind, no verse number, no letters, no Sanskrit/Roman typography, no watermark, no frame, no UI. Text will be rendered separately by the app over the image at a user-adjustable default image opacity of 48%. If Krishna is depicted, maintain a youthful calm blue-skinned figure in muted golden-yellow garments, a restrained peacock-feather crown, no modern jewelry. Arjuna is a dark-haired warrior with a small crown, bow and understated bronze armor. Use them only when the meaning warrants them; the scene or analogy remains verse-specific.  Reference (DO NOT DRAW THIS TEXT): Bhagavad Gītā 10.7. Exact Sanskrit: एतां विभूतिं योगं च मम यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः ।
सोऽविकम्पेन योगेन युज्यते नात्र संशयः ॥ ७ ॥ Exact stored meaning: He who knows, in truth, this My divine glory (vibhūti) and power (yoga) — he becomes united with Me through unwavering yoga. Of this there is no doubt. Chapter context: Divine manifestations. This chapter often names a very specific being, mountain, tree, river, season or quality. Make THAT named manifestation the dominant subject; do not default to an unrelated Krishna-Arjuna scene. Previous verse context only, do not substitute for the target: The seven great sages of old, and the four (Sanaka and his brothers) before them, and the Manus — born from My mind, imbued with My power — from them come all the creatures of the world. Next verse context only, do not substitute for the target: I am the source of all; everything proceeds from Me. Knowing this, the wise, endowed with true feeling, worship Me. Final instruction: center the distinctive content of the TARGET meaning, not the neighboring verses. No fabricated teaching or unrelated religious scene.
review_note: Contact-sheet inspection; conservative full-frame safe region preserves all figures and objects.

entry.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 10.7: He who knows, in truth, this My divine glory (vibhūti) and power (yoga) — he becomes united with Me through unwavering yoga. Of this there is no doubt.
